title: The shock ran. The door held.
dek: 2 October 2026 hourly wick from $87,249 to $83,850, the daily box since 22 September, and Farside ETF flows through the first red session and the two-day bid that followed.
thesis: A jobs print traveled in hours, not minutes. $82–83k held. One Sunday close above $86k is not acceptance.
stakes: Next evidence is a second UTC close above $86k with volume — or a close through $82k. Yields are still hostile.
subscribeHook: A second close above $86k — or a close through $82k — updates the sequence. Charts stay free here; the call moves by email.
sourceNote: Issue 29 charts use Coinbase Exchange UTC candles (hourly 2 Oct 2026; daily 22 Sep–4 Oct) and Farside Investors US-session ETF flows. 5 October is a partial UTC day and an incomplete Farside row. Weekend blanks are not zeroes. Educational scenario research; no leverage.

briefs.headline: Six hours is not ten minutes
briefs.lede: The 5-minute high $87,249 at 12:30 UTC became a $83,850 low at 18:45 UTC. $82k was not tagged.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. Peak-to-trough 3.9% in 375 minutes on Coinbase. Daily close $84,505 hid the range.

Read. Speed printed. The cascade through named gates did not.

briefs.headline: One close above $86k. Not two.
briefs.lede: 4 October closed $86,507 on 2,623 BTC. 2 October had already rejected $87,249 on 8,762 BTC.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. No completed close below $82k. Deepest probe remains 28 September $82,510.

Read. Issue 28's upgrade rule has not printed. A Sunday close is a close with an asterisk.

briefs.headline: The bid blinked, then returned
briefs.lede: 30 September −$148.7M ended the streak. 1–2 October printed +$102.7M and +$189.9M.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. Farside's completed 2 October row is +$189.9M, not the provisional +$31.7M some secondary trackers showed.

Read. One red day is not a regime. Two green days are not a new $999M impulse.
